issues.text: Attendee-step validation accepts fractional seats: entering 1.5 in Seats reserved and clicking Continue advances to Payment without a visible seats error.

Applying TEAM15 gives exactly a 15% discount and reduces the total accordingly. — With a $380.00 subtotal from the Standard and Workshop attendees, TEAM15 should discount $57.00 and produce $323.00, but after Apply the recorded Payment values remain discount −$0.00 and total $380.00 (step 24), followed by the error “That promo code is not recognised.” (step 25).

Entering fractional seats such as 1.5 is rejected with a visible seats error and does not advance to Payment. — Seats visibly contains 1.5 immediately before submission (step 36), and the following observation records that Payment is active with 2 attendees and a $165.00 total (step 37), demonstrating that the wizard advanced rather than rejecting the value.
The “Add at least one attendee” validation error remains visible after Alice is successfully added to the attendee list.
TEAM15 is rejected as unrecognised instead of applying the expected 15% discount, so the required successful-to-invalid promo replacement transition cannot be exercised.
Promo field shows TEAM15 while the visible applied-promo notice and totals still say EARLY, creating contradictory feedback.
Visible field labels are not programmatically associated: attendee name and seats appear as unnamed controls.

Validation errors disappear immediately when the Organisation and email fields become valid, and the no-attendees error disappears after an attendee is added. — After valid contact values were entered, both prior errors remained rendered (step 4); after Alice was added, “Add at least one attendee” was still visible (step 8), and the same stale attendee and seat errors persisted even with Alice and seats 1 before submission (step 44).
Inline validation error expands Profile and pushes the Notifications card down versus its initial position.
“Full name is required.” remains visible after the field contains “Progress Test User”; valid input does not clear it.
Intended literal email receipt rendering fails: unsafe is interpreted, making “unsafe” bold and omitting tags.

Bulk close after selecting all eight tickets reports "Closed 4 ticket(s)." rather than the expected "Closed 8 ticket(s)." Although all eight rows become Closed and selection clears, the toast count on

The header select-all checkbox has no effect after all tickets are closed: clicking it leaves the header and every visible ticket-row checkbox unchecked, selection at 0, and Close selected disabled. I
The header selection checkbox and all eight row selection checkboxes are exposed as unnamed checkboxes, with no visible identifying text or equivalent accessible name.
Export CSV provides visible feedback when clicked. — After the Export CSV click in step 2, step 3 recorded that the page state remained unchanged and no feedback was visible for that action.

Sending the report provides visible feedback for each Send action. — After the first Send click, step 4 recorded no visible Send feedback or dialog; after the second Send click, step 5 again showed no alert, toast, dialog, or confirmation.
The required /gridworks/report.html report path is unavailable: it returns HTTP 404 File not found instead of the weekly report.

Clicking Export CSV shows a visible “Export queued” confirmation. — After the Export CSV click, step 3's fresh inspection recorded no visible alert, toast, or confirmation message while the report and bottom-bar buttons remained visible.

Clicking Send to stakeholders shows a visible “Report sent” confirmation. — Step 4 records that both export actions had been clicked and fresh inspections immediately afterward showed no visible “Export queued” or “Report sent” confirmation.

The report is available at /gridworks/report.html and its headline Resolved figure equals the sum of all nine displayed agent Resolved values. — Navigating to /gridworks/report.html resulted in a visible 404, “File not found for /gridworks/report.html” (step 5), so the required report route and its figures could not be accessed there.
Intended literal 'Injected' text is rendered as bold 'Injected' in the booked-shift row.

Booking a valid shift with an assignee entered as Injected creates a row that displays those characters as literal text rather than rendering markup. — After the Book shift click in step 14, the observed booked-shifts area still has only the two existing rows, with no injected-assignee shift row rendered; therefore the required literal-text row was not created.

Pressing Tab from Shift date advances keyboard focus to Assign to. — After the additional Tab in step 4, the observation says Shift date remained visibly focused; step 5 likewise records that the prior Tab did not visibly move focus to Assign to.

After clicking Undo last to remove the latest Received 4 × Cable 2m movement, the stale red validation feedback “Only 26 of Cable 2m on hand.” remains visible. Inventory rollback itself is correct: Ca

Undoing the latest receipt after an invalid shipment reverts stock, totals, movement history, and clears the stale shipping-validation error. — Step 22 records that Undo correctly rolled back stock, totals, movement count, and log, but the fresh final snapshot still showed the stale validation error after the undo action.
Quantity spinbutton has no accessible name despite the visible Quantity label.

After undoing the Washer receipt, the movement log is empty. — Step 20 records that the Washer receipt was removed but an earlier Panel shipment remained; the summary also still showed 1 movement rather than an empty log.
Intended Panel A3 stepper updates decrement Cable 2m instead; Panel remains 7, blocking required non-first-item updates.
The WSH-11 “+” stepper is mapped incorrectly: clicking listed element 4 twice left WSH-11 at 60 (variance —) but incremented BLT-04 from 140 to 142 (variance +2).
The specified stock audit URL /stockroom/audit.html returns HTTP 404 File not found instead of the audit page.
